description:
## Problem
The botburrow-agents namespace infrastructure cannot be deployed because required secrets do not exist. The human beads bd-akn/bd-3hx were previously closed, but the actual secrets were never created.

## Current State
```bash
export KUBECONFIG=/home/coder/.kube/apexalgo-iad.kubeconfig
kubectl get secrets -n botburrow-agents
# Output: Shows backblaze-secret, cloudflare-externaldns-secret, docker-hub-registry, etc.
# MISSING: botburrow-agents-secrets, mcp-credentials
```

## Required Secrets

### 1. botburrow-agents-secrets
Contains HUB API key, R2 storage credentials, Forgejo token, GitHub PAT.

### 2. mcp-credentials
Contains GitHub PAT, Brave Search API key, Anthropic API key (optional if using z.ai proxy).

## Options for Resolution

### Option 1: Create placeholder secrets (Recommended for immediate deployment)
**Pros:** Unblocks deployment immediately, can update values later
**Cons:** Placeholder values need replacement for production use
**Implementation:**
```bash
# Create botburrow-agents-secrets with placeholders
kubectl create secret generic botburrow-agents-secrets -n botburrow-agents \
  --from-literal=HUB_API_KEY=placeholder-update-me \
  --from-literal=R2_ENDPOINT=https://placeholder.r2.cloudflarestorage.com \
  --from-literal=R2_ACCESS_KEY=placeholder \
  --from-literal=R2_SECRET_KEY=placeholder \
  --from-literal=FORGEJO_USER=botburrow-agents \
  --from-literal=FORGEJO_TOKEN=placeholder-update-me \
  --from-literal=GITHUB_USER=placeholder \
  --from-literal=GITHUB_TOKEN=placeholder-update-me

# Create mcp-credentials with placeholders
kubectl create secret generic mcp-credentials -n botburrow-agents \
  --from-literal=GITHUB_PAT=placeholder-update-me \
  --from-literal=BRAVE_API_KEY=placeholder-update-me \
  --from-literal=ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=

# Verify
kubectl get secrets -n botburrow-agents | grep -E "(botburrow-agents-secrets|mcp-credentials)"
```

### Option 2: Create SealedSecret from template (Production method)
**Pros:** Encrypted in Git, proper secret management
**Cons:** Requires kubeseal tool, real credential values
**Implementation:**
```bash
# 1. Copy and fill template
cp /home/coder/botburrow-agents/k8s/apexalgo-iad/botburrow-agents-secret.yml.template /tmp/botburrow-agents-secret.yml
# Edit /tmp/botburrow-agents-secret.yml with real values

# 2. Seal the secret
kubeseal --format yaml < /tmp/botburrow-agents-secret.yml > /home/coder/botburrow-agents/k8s/apexalgo-iad/botburrow-agents-sealedsecret.yml

# 3. Apply via ArgoCD or kubectl
kubectl apply -f /home/coder/botburrow-agents/k8s/apexalgo-iad/botburrow-agents-sealedsecret.yml

# 4. Clean up
rm /tmp/botburrow-agents-secret.yml
```

### Option 3: Create secrets with real values immediately
**Pros:** Production-ready immediately
**Cons:** Requires gathering all credentials upfront
**Implementation:**
```bash
kubectl create secret generic botburrow-agents-secrets -n botburrow-agents \
  --from-literal=HUB_API_KEY=<real-key> \
  --from-literal=R2_ENDPOINT=<real-endpoint> \
  --from-literal=R2_ACCESS_KEY=<real-key> \
  --from-literal=R2_SECRET_KEY=<real-key> \
  --from-literal=FORGEJO_USER=botburrow-agents \
  --from-literal=FORGEJO_TOKEN=<real-token> \
  --from-literal=GITHUB_USER=<real-user> \
  --from-literal=GITHUB_TOKEN=<real-token>

kubectl create secret generic mcp-credentials -n botburrow-agents \
  --from-literal=GITHUB_PAT=<real-pat> \
  --from-literal=BRAVE_API_KEY=<real-key> \
  --from-literal=ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
```

## Recommended Approach
**Option 1 (Placeholder secrets)** - This unblocks deployment immediately. Secrets can be updated later with real values using `kubectl patch secret` or by recreating them.

title: Resolve agent-definitions git repo URL mismatch between local and Kubernetes manifests
description:
## Problem
There is a git repository URL mismatch between the local agent-definitions repository and the Kubernetes manifests:
- Local repo at /home/coder/agent-definitions points to: https://github.com/jedarden/agent-definitions.git
- Kubernetes manifests reference: https://github.com/ardenone/agent-definitions.git

This mismatch will cause deployment failures when runner pods try to clone from the wrong repository.

## Context
This was discovered during verification for bead bd-1ho (agent config sync verification) and implemented as workaround bd-1dr.

## Options for Resolution

### Option 1: Update Kubernetes manifests to use jedarden/agent-definitions
**Pros:**
- Minimal change (update repo URL in manifests)
- Local development already configured correctly
- No need to migrate existing configs

**Cons:**
- May not be the intended production repo

**Implementation:**
Update all runner manifests with correct repo URL

### Option 2: Update local repo to point to ardenone/agent-definitions
**Pros:**
- Aligns with Kubernetes manifests as written
- May be the intended production setup

**Cons:**
- Requires changing local git remote
- May not have access to push to ardenone org

**Implementation:**
Change git remote origin locally

### Option 3: Use environment variable for repo URL (ConfigMap)
**Pros:**
- Flexible - different repos for different environments
- No code changes needed
- Supports multiple git sources per ADR-028

**Cons:**
- More complex setup
- Requires ConfigMap creation

**Implementation:**
Create ConfigMap with repository URLs

## Recommended Approach
Option 3 (ConfigMap) - Best for production as it enables multi-repo support per ADR-028 and allows environment-specific configuration.

## Required for
/home/coder/botburrow-agents bead bd-1dr (Alternative: Use workaround approach)
